correctness.rationale: Work under substitution over characteristic two. At depth d the first possible square-difference term is (d+1)a² t^(2d+1), giving exactly the even-depth obstruction and the high-depth automatic finite involutions. If the square is nontrivial with depth r, comparing f∘f² and f²∘f in degree d+r+1 shows (r-d)ab=0 for their nonzero leading coefficients a,b. Thus at odd d any first square defect has even degree. For each even n≥2d+2 the outer term indexed n-d contributes a a_(n-d); the contribution linear in that coefficient from the inner argument and leading outer term has factor d+1=0, and two insertions involving it would have degree >n. This gives one triangular condition per even degree and no other independent conditions. Changing coefficients at degrees ≥N cannot affect the square below N+d, and thereafter this same recursion imposes all even conditions and, by parity, the entire infinite involution equation. The identity jet has an infinite lift, including at arbitrarily large odd depths by the recursion. For the total finite count let h=floor(N/2), m=floor((N-1)/2). Depths d≥h plus the identity contribute q^(N-h-1); the floor(h/2) odd depths below h contribute (q-1)q^(N-2-m) each. These give all four totals, and the odd lifting exponents descend through consecutive values ending at zero. An independent truncated-Horner exact enumeration matched both depth histograms for F2 at N=3–11, F4 at N=3–7 and F8 at N=3–6. It checks the finite lifting criterion, not infinite existence; the latter is supplied by the recursion.
residual_risks: The exact iff test holds, but 'sharp' should not be read as minimal precision in every stratum: for odd N and odd d, modulus t^(N+d-1) is equivalent by parity, and some strata need no strengthened test. For F2, N=6 and d=3, t+t⁴+t⁵ has first square defect in degree 8, so modulus t^9 really is needed there.

value.rationale: The all-depth comparison answers a natural finite-quotient question that conjugacy of genuine torsion does not settle: which finite solutions are actual truncations, how many exist, and how far above the given precision one must test the square to tell. The exact criterion and quantified O(1/N) scarcity (indeed Theta(1/N)) are useful across all truncation levels and even field sizes. The rationale does not treat the later matched finite census on its own as a new contribution.
residual_risks: This is a result for one involution and characteristic two; it does not classify commuting tuples or finite quotient conjugacy classes.
